target_customer: High-transaction web, ad tech, e-commerce and gaming companies running MySQL
problem: MySQL workloads outgrew single servers and sharding was painful; customers needed a scale-out relational database.
business_model: Enterprise database software and appliances, licensing and support

founders.name: Sergei Tsarev
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Not found: education or prior employers.

technical_complexity.rationale: A distributed relational database with MySQL compatibility is research-grade systems work; product was tested at customers from 2008 and launched in 2010.

defensibility.rationale: Deep engineering and database lock-in once adopted, though open source and cloud databases later eroded the edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it directly; Amazon Aurora and other cloud databases later competed, and MariaDB acquired it in 2018, rebranded it Xpand and discontinued it in Oct 2023.

market_need_then: MySQL scale limits were a common web company pain in the late 2000s; customers named later included AOL, Nielsen and Match.

branding.domain_note: clustrix.com, redirected to MariaDB after acquisition

rebrands.why: Post-acquisition product integration; one source dates the rename to 2022

branding.community_and_virality: No sourced community or merch evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Technical enterprise brand with no evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Clustrix spent years building a scale-out MySQL-compatible database, launched it around 2010 and raised venture money through 2013, reaching about 51 staff. It was acquired by MariaDB on 2018-09-20 at an undisclosed price and later folded into Xpand, which MariaDB announced as discontinued in October 2023. A hard technical product found customers but never broke out against cloud databases.
notes: Competitors: no dated sources from around the Winter 2006 batch were found, so the list is empty. Series C 2013 conflicts (Seedtable $16.5M versus SiliconAngle treating it as earlier funding) and is not recorded. Totals vary from $45M to $71M by source. Paul Mikesell appears as a founder in search summaries but not on the YC page, so is not recorded. Xconomy Series B page returned 503, so Series B amount rests on multiple search results (VentureBeat, Xconomy, StorageNewsletter). Price undisclosed.
